records.issue_text: Interpolation tests in querySplitting.test.ts:75-86 and shardQuerySplitting.test.ts:84-99 use a mock replace function and never verify the real LokiDatasource.applyTemplateVariables interpolates step, so a real-datasource regression on step interpolation would go undetected
records.rationale: The cited new tests *do* verify step interpolation reaches execution: in `querySplitting.test.ts` they assert `...targets[0].step).toBe('5m')`, and in `shardQuerySplitting.test.ts` they similarly assert `...targets[0].step).toBe('5m')`. Since `runSplitQuery`/`runShardSplitQuery` now call `datasource.applyTemplateVariables(...)` before `runQuery`, these assertions would fail if `applyTemplateVariables` stopped interpolating `step`.

records.issue_text: shardQuerySplitting.test.ts:114 'Interpolates queries before running' asserts only that the mock `applyTemplateVariables` was invoked 5 times, not that real interpolation reached `runQuery` — the test masks a lost-return-value bug since the mock mutates in place
records.rationale: The claimed “lost-return-value bug” mechanism is contradicted by the implementation: both shardQuerySplitting.ts and querySplitting.ts use the return value of interpolation via `.map((query) => datasource.applyTemplateVariables(query, request.scopedVars, request.filters))`, so a non-mutating implementation would still work. Also, a new test in shardQuerySplitting.test.ts (`test('Interpolates queries before execution'...)`) explicitly asserts the interpolated `expr` and `step` passed into `datasource.runQuery`, so interpolation reaching `runQuery` is covered beyond just call counts.
